title: Bounded finite-projective model of ordinary affine sections
statement: Let $Y$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], with the derived categories of module sheaves and localized open sites [def-pc-derived-category]. Put $A=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. Choose a derived category of $A$-modules. Let $D$ be a cochain complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], zero above a natural degree $d$, with quasi-coherent terms, whose derived image is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex]. There exist a complex $P$ of $A$-modules and integers $a,b$ such that $P^n=0$ for $n<a$ or $b<n$, each $P^n$ is finite and projective over $A$, and $Q(P)$ is isomorphic to $Q(\Gamma(Y,D))$. Here sections are applied termwise to the actual complex $D$, and $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms.

proof.text: Put A = Gamma(Y,O) and M = the ordinary section complex of D. Choose the standard derived categories of sheaves on Spec A and its open sites. The affine derived equivalence sends Q(M) to an object E of D_QCoh, with its comparison identifying E.obj with Q(tilde(M)).

The affine section complex counit identifies pushforward of tilde(M) along Y.isoSpec.inv with D at the complex level. The localization comparison for the scheme-isomorphism equivalence then identifies its inverse image of Q(D) with Q(tilde(M)), using the inverse functor and unit. Transport perfectness through the scheme isomorphism and through this isomorphism and the affine comparison to prove that E is perfect.

Apply the affine bounded-projective characterization to E. Obtain P, bounds a,b, finite and projective terms, and E.obj isomorphic to Q(tilde(P)). Compose the inverse of this model isomorphism with the affine localization comparison at P. This is an isomorphism between the images of Q(P) and Q(M) under the fully faithful composite of the equivalence and inclusion. Its preimageIso yields Q(P) isomorphic to Q(M), retaining all bounds and term properties.
